newsitem.title: USA: Muni yields down 5-10 basis points over past week.
newsitem.headline: Muni yields down 5-10 basis points over past week.

text.p: Municipal bond yields fell an average of five to 10 basis points in the week ended Wednesday, Delphis Hanover Corp said on Friday.

After dropping five basis points in each of the last four weeks, thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields were unchanged last week at 5.45 percent. Thirty-year Baa yields were five basis points lower for the second consecutive week, at 6.20 percent.

Munis slightly outperformed Treasuries over the period, as the long bond rose two basis points to 6.43 percent from 6.41 percent in the previous week. Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis were yielding 84.8 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Wednesday, compared to 84.9 percent the week before.
Average yields on one-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds were unchanged for the third consecutive week, holding at 3.60 percent. In the Baa sector, one-year munis fell five basis points to 4.35 percent.

In the intermediate sector, ten-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds were unchanged at 4.70 percent, after dropping a total of 10 basis points over the prior two weeks. Yields on 10-year Baa-rated munis lost 10 basis points, moving to 5.50 percent.

The Aaa yield curve between one-year and 30-year municipals was unchanged at 185 basis points, after flattening five basis points in each of the prior two weeks. The spread between one-year and 30-year Baa's was unchanged at 185 basis points.

The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years narrowed five basis points to 75 basis points, after remaining unchanged for eight consecutive weeks. The 30-year spread also narrowed five to 75 basis points.
